summary: Stub package forwards to sibling dependency and ships packed Windows.node binary
details: imgdecode@1.0.2 presents itself as a native image buffer decoder but ships a 224-byte index.js whose only runtime effect on require is to load the sibling package 'imgbundle' and attempt to require./prebuilds/win32-x64/imgdecode.node, swallowing errors. The exported API is a single load() that returns null, which does not correspond to the README's advertised exec(cmd, args) interface. The bundled prebuilds/win32-x64/imgdecode.node is a 703 KB Windows PE containing a non-standard.fptable3 section and obfuscated Windows API name fragments (e.g. 'EXClos', 'E\eHan', 'EPSlee' consistent with Close/Handle/Sleep under API-name hashing or XOR-stub packing) and no normal Node-API registration symbols — characteristics of packed/obfuscated native code, not a legitimate image-decoder addon. A.node file loaded via require executes native code in the host Node process immediately on module load, so any consumer that imports imgdecode on a win32-x64 host runs the packed binary, while all other platforms silently pull in and execute whatever code the imgbundle dependency contains. The combination of a facade JS stub, a README/API mismatch, a generic throwaway author identity, and a packed Windows PE delivered via require is a dependency-forwarder plus native-dropper shape rather than a working library.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
